body:
It might be a general python problem releated to forking:
https://pythonspeed.com/articles/python-multiprocessing/

With Process `spawn` it works:

https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#contexts-and-start-methods

```python
import multiprocessing

import polars as pl


def test_sub_process(df: pl.DataFrame, job_id):
    df_filtered = df.lazy().filter(pl.col('a') > 0).collect()
    print(f"Filtered (job_id: {job_id})", df_filtered, sep="\n")


def create_dataset():
    print("Create dataset")

    test_df = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "a": [0, 2, 3, 4, 5],
            "b": [0, 4, 5, 56, 4]
        }
    )
    test_df.write_parquet("/tmp/test.parquet")


def main():
    create_dataset()

    print("Read dataset")
    test_df = pl.scan_parquet(
        "/tmp/test.parquet",
    ).collect()

    for i in range(0, 5):
        proc = multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process(
            target=test_sub_process,
            args=(test_df, i)
        )
        proc.start()
        proc.join()

        print(f"Executed sub process {i}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
Closing as this is a Python (documentation) issue, as explained in the PythonSpeed article, not a Polars issue.

I've been experiencing this as well. It does sound like this is a pitfall of `fork`, but it's often recommended to use `fork` as the start method in dataloading pipelines: https://pytorch-lightning.readthedocs.io/en/latest/accelerators/gpu_intermediate.html#distributed-data-parallel-spawn.

There's discussion here in another popular Rust library: https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/issues/187#issuecomment-651224608.

Curious on your thoughts @ritchie46 @zundertj ?

If there is such a flag, that would be useful indeed. Maybe the env variable `POLARS_MAX_THREADS`, see also #1718, works for your use case? I do see some references to that env variable in the Rust code, but there are no docs. I think [polars.threadpool_size](https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/py-polars/html/reference/api/polars.threadpool_size.html) is for getting the value used. I will leave it up to @ritchie46  to comment on specifics.

Yeah, I thought that `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=0` might fix the issue, but it still hangs on my end. I'm not too familiar with the internals of `threadpool` in `rayon`, but I'm wondering if fork-unsafe resource is being created even with `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=0`?

Perhaps here? https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/6cdc83e856d9f6576114fbf02fe5c23fd5b59d38/polars/polars-core/src/lib.rs#L47
May I ask why you want to do this in the first place? Polars is very good in thread utilization.

Thanks for the response, @ritchie46 .

The use-case is for multi-process dataloading for machine learning: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#multi-process-data-loading. There are some workarounds such as setting the start method to `forkserver` or `spawn`, but that tends to have speed implications: https://pytorch-lightning.readthedocs.io/en/latest/accelerators/gpu_intermediate.html#distributed-data-parallel-spawn.

Personally, I would really like to integrate `polars` fully into dataloading pipelines (as a replacement for `pandas` and `pyarrow`), but I'm struggling with deadlocking issues. I have no doubt that this is due to poor multiprocessing functionality in `python`, but I was wondering if there is a workaround to support this use-case?
If you load the data with polars, then there is not much benefit as polars already uses all threads. You can also use `pl.collect_all()` which executes all lazy plans in parallel.
Hmm, perhaps I'm explaining this poorly. I'm wondering if there is a way to prevent deadlocking in `polars` when launching multiple python processes via `fork`?

issue.title: Multiprocessing.Process freezes upon `pl.scan_parquet`

repository.name: polars
repository.description: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust

issue.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

Below I have a repro that generates parquet files and prints them out. When printing the contents of the parquet file in the current process it works fine, but in the subprocess it seems to be frozen for me:

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
from multiprocess import Process


def print_scanned_parquet(path):
    print("Scanning...")
    print(f"Path: {path}, df: {pl.scan_parquet(path).collect()}")


parquet_path = "/tmp/test_string_cache.parq"
df = pl.DataFrame({"a": ["foo", "bar"], "b": ["x", "y"]}).select(
    [pl.col("a").cast(pl.Categorical).alias("a"), pl.col("b").cast(pl.Categorical).alias("b")]
)
df.write_parquet(parquet_path)
print_scanned_parquet(parquet_path)
p = Process(target=print_scanned_parquet, args=(parquet_path,))
p.start()
p.join()
```


### Expected behavior

Expected the output for the `Process` to be the same. Got this instead:

```
Scanning...
Path: /tmp/test_string_cache.parq, df: shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────┐
│ a   ┆ b   │
│ --- ┆ --- │
│ cat ┆ cat │
╞═════╪═════╡
│ foo ┆ x   │
├╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ bar ┆ y   │
└─────┴─────┘
Scanning...
<stuck here>
```

body:
#5133 is a similar report.

Let me try to add to what I think @benjaminrwilson  is saying here on the use case.

People may use multiproc for a variety of reasons, not just because of Polars performance reasons, which is indeed not the way to go. Other reasons may for instance be interfacing with other libraries (PyTorch here) which do a lot of the heavy lifting, and do need/recommend multiproc for optimal performance. In those cases, Polars is just carrying around the data (in that part of the data pipeline), and users end up having the combo of multiproc + polars. It would not be nice to have to take out polars, and use something else, in the pipeline, because of that reason.
Yeah, I agree with that characterization, @zundertj . It forces me to use `pandas` in forked processes. I would prefer to use `polars`, though.

Multiprocessing is only possible in `spawned` processes. As @ghuls referred blog post shows: https://pythonspeed.com/articles/python-multiprocessing/.

This can only be solved by stopping polars from multi-threading, which is entirely out of the scope of polars. 
So to any readers of this thread that want to do multi-processing in python AND multi-threading in polars, spawn your processes.
